name: Maiadomu
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Only Ethnologue and an anonymous 2011 subclassification note; Wikipedia stub has no phonology

new_statements.quote: Maiadomu is not tonal. Stress is predictable and occurs on the penultimate syllable. The penultimate syllable is often lengthened in greetings to indicate that the speaker is happy to welcome a friend or visitor or as in Iamalele for emphasis. [p. 4] ... [tʰ] and [kʰ] occur as allophones of their unaspirated counterparts only in stressed syllables. [p. 5]
new_statements.citation: Sligh Watt, Karla. 2022. Organized Phonology Data Update: Maiadomu Language [MZZ], Milne Bay Province. Ms., 8 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives, entry 92687. Replaces Sligh & Miller 2011.
new_statements.locator: p. 4, section 'Suprasegmentals'; supporting sentence p. 5 'Phonological Conventions'
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (8 pp., native text layer, pdfinfo title 'Organized Phonology Data', created 2022-01-26). Page 4, section 'Suprasegmentals', reads exactly: 'Maiadomu is not tonal. Stress is predictable and occurs on the penultimate syllable. The penultimate syllable is often lengthened in greetings to indicate that the speaker is happy to welcome a friend or visitor or as in Iamalele for emphasis.' Page 5, 'Phonological Conventions', reads '[tʰ] and [kʰ] occur as allophones of their unaspirated counterparts only in stressed syllables.' (the text layer encodes the aspiration glyphs in a legacy SIL IPA93 font as private-use codepoints, so extracted text prints '[tand [', but the rendered page, checked…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is not contrastive and falls on the penultimate syllable of the word; the language has no tone. Aspiration of /t/ and /k/ is confined to stressed syllables. The penult can additionally be lengthened as an expressive device (greetings, emphasis).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Note that the OPD also reports syncope/apocope of high vowels after nasals (kom(u), kan(i), sim(u)sim(u)) with the underlying CV form retained; the source does not say how this interacts with penultimate stress. p. 6 says a hyphen is written before adverbial suffixes to help readers place stress on the correct syllable, implying the stress domain includes suffixed forms.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (the OPD is a phonological-word sketch; no phrase-level statement). Data checked by the same SIL fieldworker; an 8-page organized-phonology-data sheet, not a full grammar.
new_statements.identity_note: The source is titled 'Maiadomu Language [MZZ]' (SIL archive subject language Maiadomu [mzz] = Glottolog maia1251), with villages Madagowai, Subita, Yavalai, Kubwana, Wasalia, Mekuya, Kalokaloye, Dodobutu, Sigamwana and Niumole on Fergusson Island; no dialect distinction is made. Glottolog's 'Anonymous 2011, Maiadom Organised Phonology Data' is the earlier version of this same SIL OPD (Sligh & Miller 2011, entry 42254).
